analysis.title: GS TMT SPEC SALES: SAP & META beat; TXN +ve Analog; BESI pushes back; TELIA solid; RELX solid; PSON inline; NOKIA debate
key_insights: US equities rose overnight. QQQ gained 1.1% and semis outperformed by 2.2% on positive updates from SpaceX and Super Micro and constructive AI commentary, though the rebound felt modest after recent weakness. Software gained 1.8%, led by cybersecurity stocks after an AI-discovered PHP vulnerability.
Asia did not follow the US rebound. KOSPI fell about 3.5%, China is flirting with a bear market, and the semiconductor complex was weak.

Most results overnight and this morning were solid. Meta, SAP, TXN and IBM beat expectations. LRCX, Nokia, BESI and Pearson were respectable but softer guidance or high expectations limited upside. Telia and RELX were steady.

Meta did not raise capex but did not answer the question on 2027 capex intensity, pushing it to the Q4 call. It also did not address SpaceX's point that power, cooling and electrical infrastructure, rather than chips alone, constrain AI deployment.

Meta beat with revenue above the top of guidance and advertising growth of 26%, despite a $9.9bn one-off legal settlement. Q4 revenue guidance of $73-76bn brackets consensus of $73.6bn and the roughly $75bn buyside bar. 2026 capex guidance was tightened to $135-145bn from $130-145bn. The shares were up 3% after hours.

Meta's Muse product has about 10mn downloads and strong shopping usage, but monetisation is still developing and capacity is constrained. Reality Labs losses are expected to decline toward roughly $15bn.

SAP current cloud backlog (CCB) grew 26% at constant currency versus consensus of 24.6% and a buyside bar of at least 25%. Organic CCB growth of about 25.2% showed no deceleration for a third straight quarter. The shares were up about 3.5-4% in the US after hours.

SAP cloud revenue rose 25% to roughly €6.7bn, about two points ahead of expectations, helped by about one point of one-off benefits. Total revenue was €10.27bn and operating profit €3.03bn, both ahead. FY26 cloud revenue is now expected toward the top of the €25.8-26.2bn range, with operating profit and free-cash-flow guidance unchanged.

SAP's CFO said on the call that there are early signs higher interest rates are affecting customer behaviour. Q4 is still expected to decelerate with no clarity on scale. The author thinks street CCB estimates will trickle up from 23% constant currency.

TXN delivered a strong Q3 with revenue, gross margin and operating margin ahead. Industrial and automotive were each up about 10% quarter on quarter and data-centre revenue grew 20%. Q4 guidance midpoints are revenue of $6.05bn and EPS of $2.62, well above typical seasonality.

TXN trailing-12-month free cash flow rose to $8.4bn from $2.4bn a year earlier, suggesting the heavy capex cycle is largely behind it. This is the first read-through to the analog group including IFX and STM. TXN's gross-margin recovery may lag Microchip and NXP, where near-term earnings revisions could be stronger.

BESI is mixed. The quarter was solid with small gross and operating profit beats and orders 15% ahead of the street. The Q4 guide is light because customers pushed out deliveries to align with H1-27 capacity plans. Revenue is guided flat to +/-5% versus Q3-26 against street +4%. Management pushed back on concerns that ASML could compete in die-to-wafer hybrid bonding. The author expects the stock up today given consensus short positioning.

LRCX fell 7.5% after an in-line quarter and an outlook below elevated expectations. Q4 revenue guidance of $8.60bn compares with the Street at $8.62bn and GS at $8.87bn. China rebounded to 35% of revenue from 26%. Lam raised its 2026 WFE forecast to the mid-$150bn range and guided to more than $200bn in 2027.

IBM rose 6%. Software revenue growth accelerated to 9% year on year at constant currency from 5%, Transaction Processing grew 10% from a 9% decline, and Red Hat/Hybrid Cloud grew 11%. IBM reiterated 4-5% full-year constant-currency revenue growth and raised free-cash-flow guidance to growth of more than $1bn.

Nokia is mixed. Q3 net sales were €5.15bn, 2% above consensus, and comparable EBIT was €605mn, 34% above. FY26 comparable EBIT guidance of €2.1-2.6bn was only reiterated, implying street Q4 is too high. Nokia guided optical and IP Networks to grow 25-30% in 2027 versus the street at 20%. AI and cloud orders were €1.5bn, down quarter on quarter from €2.8bn in Q2.

Telia raised guidance but the street is already there. Service revenue was 1.2% ahead and EBITDA 0.9% ahead. FY adjusted EBITDA growth is now seen at 3-4% like for like and free operating cash flow at least SEK9bn. Telia is more constructive on Sweden than Tele2 and pushed back on Telenor's claims of higher competition in Norway.

Pearson Q3 organic growth was 6% versus street 5.5%, driven by virtual schools and Assessment & Qualifications (+10%, AI contract signed in July). Higher Ed and ELL looked light, and Higher Ed guidance was trimmed from >2% to >0%. The author is unsure this is enough given the run in the shares and valuation. Adjusted operating profit guidance was narrowed to £650-675mn.
RELX had no surprises. 9M organic growth was 7%, in line with GSe, and FY26 guidance was reiterated. Exhibitions grew 4% versus GSe 4.4%.

A critical PHP flaw led European government agencies and organisations to take websites offline. Hackers were already exploiting it. PHP powers roughly 75% of websites with an identifiable programming language. A fix is released but automatic WordPress updates do not patch the server software.
An a16z letter says token demand will rise 24x from 2026 to 2030 while available power rises only about 2x, so scarcity in physical infrastructure is likely.

Meta was ordered to pay New Mexico $25bn after a Cambridge Analytica privacy trial, below the $35-40bn requested but above the $18bn settlement agreed by 48 other states in August. Meta plans to appeal.
AWS reportedly planned to receive US$5bn of GB300 racks upfront then about US$3bn monthly, with some equipment stored in warehouses because data centers lack power.

Lenovo, HP and Dell reportedly signed memory long-term agreements for 2027 supply after DRAM/SSD deliveries met only 70-80% of demand last year. Omdia reportedly puts 3Q26 PC shipments down 21% YoY with a further 7% decline forecast for 2027, and PC prices could rise 10-20%.

Elisa's call suggested a weaker near-term outlook. Full-year telecom service revenue growth is tracking toward the low end of 0-2% guidance, with downside risk to consensus of +0.2%. Year-to-date cash flow is down 12% and leverage is 1.9x versus a 1.5-2.0x range.

AT&T missed on postpaid phone net additions of 379k, about 10k below consensus. It cut 2027 and 2028 capital investment to $22-23bn from $23-24bn, a negative read-through for Ericsson. US telcos fell on SpaceX comments on a US mobile network.

US trading was boosted by momentum chasing in high-velocity names, with more than 1m SPCX call options traded. Mag7 lagged on competition concerns after SPCX results, rotation into SPCX, Cleveland checks weighing on GOOGL, and possible source-of-funds selling ahead of expected future issuance. Semis bounced after 10 of 11 sessions lower. Hedge funds were small net buyers and asset managers were flat.

sector_views.rationale: TXN results confirm a broadening analog recovery and should support a positive initial reaction across the sector including IFX and STM.
SAP and IBM show healthy enterprise software demand, but SAP's CFO flagged early signs that higher rates affect customer behaviour.
Telia is steady and Elisa is weaker, while US telcos fell on SpaceX mobile plans and AT&T lowered capex.

earnings_insights: Meta Q3 2026 reported: revenue above the top end of guidance, advertising growth 26%, results include a $9.9bn one-off legal settlement. Q4 guidance $73-76bn versus consensus $73.6bn. 2026 capex guidance $135-145bn from $130-145bn.

SAP Q3 2026 reported: CCB +26% cc versus consensus 24.6%, cloud revenue about €6.7bn (+25%), total revenue €10.27bn, operating profit €3.03bn. FY26 cloud revenue guided toward the top of €25.8-26.2bn.
TXN Q3 2026 reported: revenue, gross margin and operating margin ahead. Q4 guidance midpoints (company guide, above street) revenue $6.05bn and EPS $2.62.
BESI Q3-26 reported: orders 15% ahead of the street, operating expenses €55.1mn. Q4 guide (company guide): revenue flat +/-5% versus Q3-26 against street +4%, gross margin 63-65%, opex up 5-10%.

LRCX reported: F2Q gross margin 52.4% versus consensus around 52%. Q4 guide (company guide): revenue $8.60bn at the midpoint versus Street $8.62bn and GS $8.87bn, EPS $2.33 at the midpoint in line with consensus.

IBM reported: software revenue +9% constant currency versus +5% last quarter. FY constant-currency revenue growth outlook of 4-5% reiterated, free-cash-flow guidance raised to growth of more than $1bn.

Nokia Q3 reported: net sales €5.15bn (+2% versus consensus), comparable EBIT €605mn (+34% versus consensus). Q4 guide (company): sales +20-24% qoq versus consensus +26%. FY26 comparable EBIT guide €2.1-2.6bn versus consensus €2.398bn.

Telia Q3 reported: service revenue 1.2% ahead, EBITDA 0.9% ahead. Raised guide (company): FY adjusted EBITDA growth 3-4% like for like versus street 3.4%, free operating cash flow at least SEK9bn versus consensus SEK9.27bn.

Pearson Q3 reported: organic growth 6% versus street 5.5%. FY guide reiterated at mid-single-digit organic growth versus GSe +4.6% and consensus +4.7%/+4.8%. Adjusted operating profit guide narrowed to £650-675mn.
RELX 9M reported: organic growth 7% in line with GSe, Exhibitions 4% versus GSe 4.4%.
AT&T reported: postpaid phone net adds 379k, about 10k below consensus. 2026 FCF above $18bn reiterated, 2026 adjusted EBITDA growth at the upper end of 3-4%.
crypto_views: Coinbase moved its media agency from WPP's Wavemaker to the independent shop Noble People as it expands beyond cryptocurrency.
risk_factors: Meta's rising capital intensity leaves 2027 spending, compute efficiency and returns on the AI build-out unresolved until the Q4 call.
Power, cooling and electrical infrastructure constrain AI deployment, as shown by AWS GB300 racks stored in warehouses.
SAP's pace of CCB deceleration into year-end and early signs that higher rates affect customer behaviour.
Elevated expectations after recent beats limited upside for LRCX, Nokia and BESI.
Possible source-of-funds trading ahead of expected SPCX issuance weighing on Mag7.
The PHP vulnerability is being actively exploited and may leave smaller organisations exposed for longer.
Memory supply shortfalls and rising PC prices, with Omdia forecasting a further 7% PC shipment decline in 2027.
vol_and_positioning: BESI is described as a consensus short, and the author expects it to rise today given positioning.
More than 1m SPCX call options traded in the US session, with momentum chasing in high-velocity pockets.
Semis bounced after 10 of 11 sessions lower but felt underwhelming.

Hedge funds finished as small net buyers, driven by tech, healthcare and financials, against supply in communication services. Asset manager flows were roughly flat, with demand in financials/REITs, industrials and energy against supply in utilities, healthcare and tech.
The GS floor activity was a 5 on a 1-10 scale, finishing +3% better to buy on muted notional.
